title: Sable and the Playlist
premise: Tamsin Winterbourne has spent senior year perfecting the art of silence at home, where her father's campaign for district judge demands a flawless family image. When debate teacher Ms. Okonkwo pairs her with Sable Reyes — the transfer student who publicly humiliated her last fall — on a semester project documenting a wrongful conviction, Tamsin discovers the convicted man is her father's old client, and clearing his name means exposing her family. As she and Sable dig through sealed records and buried testimony, their rivalry thaws into something neither will name, even as her father's campaign manager begins erasing evidence faster than they can find it. In the end, Tamsin testifies at the clemency hearing, sacrificing her father's career and her own spot at her dream college to tell the truth — and chooses Sable, and justice, over the version of loyalty she was raised on.
about_author: Sebastian Voss is the pen name of a former high school debate coach who spent seven years watching teenagers argue beautifully about everything except themselves. He writes in a converted garage in Portland, Oregon, where his own teenage daughter fact-checks every draft.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. After another silent dinner dominated by her father's judge campaign, Tamsin walks into debate class expecting routine — instead Ms. Okonkwo pairs her with Sable Reyes, her nemesis since his brutal takedown of her at the fall invitational. Their first project meeting is pure friction until Sable reveals his topic: Marcus Bell, a man convicted of arson twelve years ago. The emotional beat: reluctant curiosity cracking open old hostility.

chapters.title: Sealed Records
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Tamsin and Sable. Digging through courthouse archives, they discover Bell's defense attorney was Tamsin's father — who suppressed an eyewitness statement that would have won acquittal. Tamsin secretly photographs the file while Sable wonders why she keeps going pale. At home, her father announces his campaign has 'big news coming.' The emotional beat: dread blooming as duty and truth begin pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, then Tamsin's. The campaign manager confronts Tamsin with photos of her and Sable breaking into the records annex, offering a deal: drop the project, keep her father's future intact. She almost signs — until Sable, feeling betrayed by her hesitation, shows up at her house and forces a confrontation her parents witness. That night, Tamsin finds the missing eyewitness statement hidden in her father's study. The emotional beat: the friendship fractures just as love becomes undeniable.

chapters.title: The Last Argument
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the clemency hearing, with her father watching from the gallery, Tamsin delivers the argument of her life — not to win a trophy, but to free Marcus Bell, submitting the suppressed statement and her father's role in burying it. Bell walks out; her father's career collapses; her acceptance letter is rescinded days later. On the courthouse steps, Sable waits with two coffees and no speech. The emotional beat: grief and freedom arriving together, and choosing both.
